name: Scientist
hook: A teenager who started out repairing King Tubby's electronics ended up in his engineer's chair, and gave dub its horror-movie phase.

blurb.age7: Scientist was a teenager who learned to fix electronics at King Tubby's studio, then learned to mix records there too. He later made dub albums with spooky, science-fiction names.
blurb.age13: Hopeton 'Overton' Brown, who took the name Scientist, started out around King Tubby's Waterhouse studio as a teenager in the mid-1970s, repairing equipment before he was allowed near the mixing desk. By the early 1980s he was one of Tubby's two lead engineers, alongside Prince Jammy, and mixed a run of dub albums under themed titles like 'Scientist Rids the World of the Evil Curse of the Vampires' (1981), built from rhythms recorded at Channel One by the Roots Radics band.
blurb.adult: Scientist's career traces the handoff of dub production from King Tubby personally to a next generation of engineers he trained, a transition also carried by Prince Jammy. His early-1980s albums kept Tubby's mixing techniques current for a new set of Kingston studios and bands (Channel One, the Roots Radics) after the scene's founding studios had moved on, and their horror-and-science-fiction theming packaged an already established musical approach as a recognisable brand.

signatureTracks.title: Scientist Rids the World of the Evil Curse of the Vampires
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The title track and album that made his themed-album format famous, mixed at King Tubby's studio.
